questions.prompt: Which C# type is used to store whole numbers like -5, 0, or 42?
questions.explanation: int is used for 32-bit signed integers. double is for decimals, bool for true/false, and string for text.

questions.prompt: What is the default value of an unassigned int field?
Arrange these numeric types from smallest to largest
questions.explanation: short (2 bytes) < int (4 bytes) < long (8 bytes) < double (8 bytes).

questions.prompt: Which type represents sequences of characters (text)?
questions.explanation: string represents a sequence of characters. char is a single character.

questions.prompt: Declare variables of type int, double, and bool, initialize them, and print each on its own line
What is the size of a double in C#?
questions.explanation: double is a 64-bit floating-point type, so it uses 8 bytes.

questions.prompt: What is the default value of a char variable?
Which type can hold the value null by default in C#?
questions.explanation: string is a reference type and defaults to null. int, bool, and char are value types with non-null defaults.

questions.prompt: Arrange these types from smallest to largest default memory usage
questions.explanation: char (2 bytes) < int (4 bytes) < double (8 bytes) < string (reference type with object header).

questions.prompt: Which of these is a value type in C#?
questions.explanation: int is a value type stored on the stack (usually). string, arrays, and classes are reference types.
